screen1-a1.expectation: It opens the side menu with the list of sections.

screen1-a2.where: the outlined ghost face at the top right
screen1-a2.expectation: I do not know. A ghost is not an action. Maybe something to do with hiding, or something 'spooky'. I cannot tell from this screen.
screen1-a2.cue: Nothing. There is no word next to it; it is a picture of a ghost.

first_pass.why: A ghost represents an idea, not a thing I can name as an action. Nothing on this screen tells me what pressing it does.
first_pass.solution: Put a text label next to it, for example 'Incognito chat', or at least show the words when I hold my finger on it.

test_cases.targets: whether anything tells you what the ghost does before it changes the screen, or only afterwards
test_cases.action: Start from the main screen (the one with the typing box at the bottom). If you are not there, press the three lines at the top left and then 'New chat'. Hold your finger on the ghost at the top right for about a second and watch for any words. Then read what the screen now says. To go back, press the same corner control again.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: no words name it before anything changes, and you only find out what it did after it has done it
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: words appear (on holding, or near it) that tell you what it does before anything changes
test_cases.what_happened: I held my finger on the ghost at the top right of the main screen for about a second. No words appeared. First a grey circle showed behind the ghost, then the screen switched straight to 'Incognito chat', with the filled ghost and the sentence about incognito chats staying out of history. So holding it did not explain it; it just did it. I only learned what it was after it had already changed the screen. I pressed the X in the same corner to go back.

screen1-a2.closing_comment: Holding the ghost gave no words. It went straight to incognito, so I could only learn what it does by doing it. That is worse than I expected.

test_cases.targets: which kind of adding the plus does (a file, a new chat, a project)
